compiled_state.description:
# The defect

`infra/scripts/observability.sh` resolves the two newest cap scripts as siblings of the
RUNNING probe, using their REPOSITORY basename:

```
 999: VARTMP_CAP_SH="${VARTMP_CAP_SH:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/vartmp-cap.sh}"
1092: CONTAINER_CAP_SH="${CONTAINER_CAP_SH:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/container-cap.sh}"
```

`install-observability.sh:12` installs the probe as `/usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh`,
so `dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"` is `/usr/local/bin` and those expand to
`/usr/local/bin/vartmp-cap.sh` and `/usr/local/bin/container-cap.sh`.

**Nothing ever creates those two paths.** `install-observability.sh` installs ONLY
`observability.sh`. The scripts' own `--install` self-installs under a DIFFERENT,
`rebar-`-prefixed name:

```
infra/scripts/vartmp-cap.sh:121    VAR_TMP_INSTALLED_PATH="${...:-/usr/local/bin/rebar-vartmp-cap.sh}"
infra/scripts/container-cap.sh:124 CONTAINER_INSTALLED_PATH="${...:-/usr/local/bin/rebar-container-cap.sh}"
```

So the name the probe looks for and the name the installer writes can never be the same file.
This is a naming mismatch, not a missing deploy step.

## Proven on the host, both before and after the reapers were installed

On i-00880b2c7f13527c5 the probe's two invocations failed with **rc 127**:

```
bash: /usr/local/bin/vartmp-cap.sh: No such file or directory     vartmp_printenv_rc=127
bash: /usr/local/bin/container-cap.sh: No such file or directory  container_printenv_rc=127
```

1. **Two cap-compliance percentages are never published.** `--print-env` produces no output, so
   `VAR_TMP_MAX_BYTES` / `CONTAINER_WRITABLE_BYTES` stay unset and the budget guards at
   `observability.sh:1037` and `:1118` are false. `var_tmp_used_percent` and
   `container_writable_used_percent` are absent from the `rebar/host` namespace entirely, and
   `rebar-var-tmp-usage-high` / `rebar-container-writable-usage-high` had **0 datapoints in 3h**.

2. **Both heartbeats are pinned to 0 regardless of the true state.** `--check-active` returns an
   empty string, which `case` coerces to `0`, so `var_tmp_cleanup_active` and
   `container_reaper_active` publish 0 whether or not a reaper runs. Both dead-man alarms read
   12/12 datapoints at 0.00.

The decisive evidence is what happened after `vartmp-cap.sh --install` and
`container-cap.sh --install` were run on the host at 2026-09-06 01:23Z. Both reaper timers are
now in force, and the scripts answer 1 at their INSTALLED names — while the names the probe
actually calls still do not exist:

```
# truth, via the installed (prefixed) path
vartmp_true=[1]      container_true=[1]
# what the probe calls
bash: /usr/local/bin/vartmp-cap.sh: No such file or directory
bash: /usr/local/bin/container-cap.sh: No such file or directory
```

So a host with BOTH reapers correctly installed still publishes `0` for both heartbeats and
still omits both percentages. Repairing the host does not repair the metric; only this
resolution change does.

The other two cap scripts are a natural control. `docker-storage-cap.sh` and `journald-cap.sh`
are present at `/usr/local/bin` (neither defines an `INSTALLED_PATH`, so their repo basename is
the only name they have), and their percentages — `docker_storage_used_percent`,
`journal_used_percent` — publish normally. Presence at the probe-sibling path is exactly what
separates the working pair from the broken pair, 4 for 4.

Existing tests do not catch this because `tests/scripts/test_observability_var_tmp.py` runs
`infra/scripts/observability.sh` in place, where the repo sibling `vartmp-cap.sh` IS present.
The test layout is the checkout layout and never the installed layout.

## What this is hiding

`/var/tmp` measured 3664 MiB against the 4 GiB budget `--print-env` reports — about **89%**,
above the 85% threshold of `rebar-var-tmp-usage-high`. The alarm that cannot see its metric
would be firing on a true condition if it could.

## Not the cause

The probe is CURRENT: `sha256(/usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh)` equals
`sha256(origin/main infra/scripts/observability.sh)` = `6d900dbde913...`, so the truncation fix
`aaa31f11f3bc` is deployed. `probe_ok` and `probe_truncated` publish normally, so this is
neither probe staleness nor truncation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `observability.sh` resolves each cap script through an ordered candidate list that
      includes the name its own `--install` writes (`/usr/local/bin/rebar-vartmp-cap.sh`,
      `/usr/local/bin/rebar-container-cap.sh`) and the repo-sibling name
      (`vartmp-cap.sh`, `container-cap.sh`), picking the first that exists, so the installed
      host and the checkout both resolve. Checked by
      `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_var_tmp.py tests/scripts/test_observability_container_layers.py`.
- [ ] The `VARTMP_CAP_SH` / `CONTAINER_CAP_SH` environment overrides still take precedence over
      every candidate, so tests injecting a stub path are unaffected. Checked by the existing
      cases in the two suites above, which set those variables and must still pass.
- [ ] A regression test proves the installed-name layout resolves: with only
      `rebar-vartmp-cap.sh` beside the probe and no `vartmp-cap.sh`, a probe run publishes
      `var_tmp_used_percent` and `var_tmp_cleanup_active=1`; the equivalent holds for
      `container_writable_used_percent` and `container_reaper_active`. Reverting the resolution
      change must fail this test.
- [ ] A test proves the coupling cannot silently break again: the candidate list in
      `observability.sh` contains the `*_INSTALLED_PATH` default declared in `vartmp-cap.sh`
      and `container-cap.sh`, so renaming an installed path without updating the probe fails
      the build. Checked by that test failing when either default is edited in isolation.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_var_tmp.py -x` — the /var/tmp probe suite, extended
  with the installed-name layout case.
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_container_layers.py -x` — same for the writable
  container-layer probe.
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_vartmp_cap.py tests/scripts/test_container_cap.py -x` — proves the
  `*_INSTALLED_PATH` defaults this change couples to are unchanged.
- `make lint && make typecheck` — the commit gate.
- Post-deploy verification on the host: after the change lands and autodeploy re-materializes
  the probe, `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace rebar/host --metric-name
  var_tmp_used_percent` returns datapoints, and `var_tmp_cleanup_active` reads 1 rather than 0.

## Out of scope (filed separately)

That `docker-storage-cap.sh` / `journald-cap.sh` are present at `/usr/local/bin` only by manual
operator copy — no repo path installs them there — is tracked on
`kittenish-venomous-pittabird` (`0bdf-b496-7201-4c84`).

file_impact.reason: Resolve VARTMP_CAP_SH and CONTAINER_CAP_SH through an ordered candidate list that includes the installed rebar- prefixed name, not only the repo-sibling basename.
Add the installed-name layout regression case: only rebar-vartmp-cap.sh beside the probe must still publish var_tmp_used_percent and var_tmp_cleanup_active=1.
Same installed-name layout regression case for container_writable_used_percent and container_reaper_active.

compiled_state.title: The probe resolves the /var/tmp and container cap scripts by a name nothing ever installs, so two cap-compliance percentages are permanently off the air and both heartbeats read 0 on any host
